changes.source_excerpt: [F7] Each finite-dimensional normed space $Z_N$ is complete; a contraction of a closed ball in $Z_N$ has a unique fixed point.
changes.proposed_replacement: [F7] Each finite-dimensional normed space $Z_N$ is complete ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]]). A closed ball in $Z_N$ is complete: every Cauchy sequence in the ball converges in $Z_N$, and continuity of the norm keeps its limit in the ball. A contraction of a nonempty closed ball into itself therefore has a unique fixed point by [[thm-banach-fixed-point]].

supplier_reading.actual_claim: Finite ordered basis over R or C implies Banach; real finite-dimensional Z_N satisfies it. Its proof includes zero-dimensional spaces.
A nonempty complete metric selfmap with contraction factor 0<=q<1 has exactly one fixed point; the local KKT proof already establishes a closed-ball selfmap with factor<=1/2.
